docs.title: Data Setup
docs.text: This project supports KITTI “mini” subset (50 images) and nuScenes v1.0-mini (official mini split).

docs.title: KITTI “mini” Subset
docs.text:
1. Download raw KITTI data
  2. Visit KITTI dataset page.

  3. Download images and Velodyne point clouds from raw data.

  4. Extract and organize

  5. Unpack to this structure: <KITTI_ROOT>/ ├── image_2/ └── velodyne/

  6. Update datasets/config.yaml: yaml kitti: root: /absolute/path/to/<KITTI_ROOT>

  7. Generate the 50-image subset

  8. Run: bash poetry run python scripts/create_kitti_subset.py 50
  9. Creates under datasets/:
    • kitti50/images/
    • kitti50/labels/
    • kitti50.yaml
  10. Note: The script subsamples the raw KITTI data.

docs.title: nuScenes v1.0-mini
docs.text:
1. Download the mini split
  2. Visit nuScenes download page.

  3. Or use: bash wget https://www.nuscenes.org/data/v1.0-mini.tgz tar xzf v1.0-mini.tgz

  4. Place the folder

  5. Move v1.0-mini/ to: av-perception/datasets/v1.0-mini/

  6. Update the config

  7. In datasets/config.yaml: yaml nuscenes: root: v1.0-mini

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: This project requires Python 3.11 and uses Poetry for dependency management.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Ensure Python 3.11 is installed bash python3.11 --version

  2. Install Poetry (if not already installed) bash curl -sSL https://install.python-poetry.org | python3.11 - export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

  3. Note: Verify with poetry --version.

  4. Clone the repository and install dependencies bash git clone https://github.com/<your-org>/av-perception.git cd av-perception poetry install

  5. (Optional) Activate the virtual environment bash poetry shell

docs.title: Development Tools
docs.text: These tools are included for development: - MkDocs: Generates the documentation site. bash poetry add --dev mkdocs mkdocs-material mkdocstrings[python] - Streamlit: Powers the web dashboard. bash poetry add streamlit matplotlib opencv-python - MLflow: Logs training experiments (included in dependencies).

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
After installation, check: 

poetry run python --version  # Should be Python 3.11.x
poetry run pip freeze       # List installed packages

docs.title: Live Playback Demo
docs.text: Streams camera and LiDAR data, performs 2D detection, fuses to 3D, tracks objects, and displays results in real-time.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# Inside the Poetry shell
python scripts/main.py [--duration <seconds>] [--interval <sec>]
# Or without the shell
poetry run python scripts/main.py --duration 30 --interval 0.05

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --duration <seconds>: Total run time (default: 10.0).
  • --interval <sec>: Sleep between frames, controls frame rate (default: 0.05, ~20 Hz).
  • DATASET_NAME: Set via environment variable ("kitti" or "nuscenes", default: "kitti").

docs.title: What Happens
docs.text:
1. DataStreamer: Loads frames and point clouds.
  2. Detector: Runs YOLO for 2D detection.
  3. FusionEngine: Projects LiDAR to refine detections.
  4. SimpleTracker: Assigns track IDs.
  5. Overlay: Shows camera view with boxes, IDs, and FPS.

  6. Console: Prints frame stats.

  7. Note: Press q to exit early.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Follow these steps to get the AV-Perception demo up and running quickly.

  1. Clone the repository bash git clone https://github.com/<your-org>/av-perception.git cd av-perception

  2. Install dependencies with Poetry bash poetry install # (Optional) Spawn a shell: poetry shell

  3. Download datasets

  4. See Data Setup for full instructions on preparing the KITTI and nuScenes datasets.

  5. Note: The default dataset is KITTI.

  6. Run the live playback demo bash # Inside the Poetry shell python scripts/main.py --duration 30 --interval 0.1 # Or without the shell poetry run python scripts/main.py --duration 30 --interval 0.1

  7. --duration: Total run time in seconds.
  8. --interval: Sleep time between frames (controls frame rate).
  9. Note: Press q in the OpenCV window to quit early.

  10. To switch datasets (e.g., to nuScenes): bash DATASET_NAME=nuscenes poetry run python scripts/main.py

  11. (Optional) Launch the web dashboard bash poetry run streamlit run scripts/web_dashboard.py

  12. Open http://localhost:8501 in your browser.

docs.title: Web Dashboard
docs.text: A Streamlit-based dashboard for real-time perception metrics and visualization.

docs.title: Launch
docs.text:
1. Ensure dependencies are installed bash poetry add streamlit matplotlib opencv-python

  2. Run the app bash poetry run streamlit run scripts/web_dashboard.py

  3. Open in browser

  4. Visit http://localhost:8501 (default Streamlit port).

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Sequence Selector: Choose KITTI Clear-Day or nuScenes Rain-Night.
  • Enable LiDAR Fusion: Toggle fusion on/off.
  • Run Duration (s): Set demo length.
  • Refresh Interval (ms): Control update frequency.
  • 2D / 3D Metrics: Real-time monitoring.
  • Overlay: Camera view with boxes and tracks.
  • Top-down LiDAR Scatter: LiDAR point cloud plot.

docs.title: Code Highlights
docs.text:
# In scripts/web_dashboard.py
@st.cache_resource
def init_streamer(...): ...
@st.cache_resource
def init_detector(...): ...
...
c1, c2, c3 = st.columns(3)
m2d = c1.metric("2D Detections", 0)
...

docs.title: yolo_pipeline.io.data_streamer
docs.text: Play back KITTI or nuScenes as a live RGB+LiDAR stream.

docs.title: Module overview
docs.text: Reads dataset images and pointclouds in a background thread, exposes latest frame via getters.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from yolo_pipeline.io.data_streamer import DataStreamer
import time

ds = DataStreamer("datasets/config.yaml")
ds.load_split("kitti", split="train", shuffle=False)
ds.start()
time.sleep(0.2)

frame = ds.get_latest_camera_frame()
pc = ds.get_latest_pointcloud()
print(frame.shape, pc.shape)

ds.stop()

docs.title: yolo_pipeline.perception.detector
docs.text: Wrapper around Ultralytics YOLO for easy 2D detection.

docs.title: Module overview
docs.text:
Provides a simple Detector class that: - Loads a YOLO model by path or name. - Moves it to a specified device. - Runs inference on NumPy images, returning plain Python dicts.

from yolo_pipeline.perception.detector import Detector
import numpy as np

det = Detector(model_path="yolov8n.pt", device="cpu")
det.load_model()
img = np.zeros((640,640,3), dtype=np.uint8)
preds = det.predict(img, conf=0.3, iou=0.5)
print(preds)

docs.title: __init__(model_path: str = "yolov8n.pt", device: str = "cpu")
docs.text:
• model_path: YOLO model name or path to a .pt file.
  • device: Inference device string (e.g. "cpu", "0").

docs.title: load_model(model_path: str = None) -> None
docs.text: Loads YOLO model and moves it to the specified device.

docs.title: predict(image: np.ndarray, conf: float = 0.25, iou: float = 0.45) -> List[Dict[str,Any]]
docs.text: Runs YOLO detection and returns list of detections with bounding box, confidence, and class ID.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
img = np.zeros((256,256,3), dtype=np.uint8)
det = Detector("yolov8n.pt", "cpu")
det.load_model()
preds = det.predict(img, conf=0.1, iou=0.5)

docs.title: yolo_pipeline.perception.fusion
docs.text: Sensor fusion: project 2D boxes into 3D using LiDAR.

docs.title: Module overview
docs.text: FusionEngine projects 2D detections onto a 3D point cloud, scores and filters them.

docs.title: __init__(camera_intrinsics: Dict[str,Any], extrinsics: Dict[str,Any], min_points: int = 3)
docs.text: Initializes with camera intrinsics and extrinsics, stores min_points threshold.

docs.title: fuse(detections: List[Dict], pointcloud: np.ndarray) -> List[Dict]
docs.text: Projects LiDAR points to image space and matches against 2D boxes. Returns filtered and rescored detections.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from yolo_pipeline.perception.fusion import FusionEngine
import numpy as np

intr = {"fx":1,"fy":1,"cx":0,"cy":0}
ext = {"R": np.eye(3), "T": [0,0,0]}
engine = FusionEngine(intr, ext, min_points=2)

dets = [{"box":[10,20,100,120], "confidence":0.8, "class_id":0}]
pc = np.array([[50,60,5,0.],[15,30,2,0.],[200,200,1,0.]], dtype=float)
fused = engine.fuse(dets, pc)
print(fused)

docs.title: yolo_pipeline.perception.tracker
docs.text: Simple 3D tracker skeleton and Detection3D dataclass.

docs.title: Module overview
docs.text:
• Detection3D: Data class for detection with ID and metadata.
  • Sort: Dummy tracker assigning new ID every frame.
  • SimpleTracker: Wrapper that emits Detection3D from fused detection dicts.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from yolo_pipeline.perception.tracker import SimpleTracker

fused_dets = [{"box":[0,0,10,10],"class_id":0,"confidence":0.5,"num_points":5,"depth":2.1}]
tracker = SimpleTracker()
tracks = tracker.update(fused_dets)

for t in tracks:
    print(f"ID={t.track_id}, class={t.class_id}, depth={t.depth}, pts={t.num_points}")

docs.title: benchmark_official.py
docs.text: Run eval.py on one or more official YOLO model variants (e.g. yolov8s, yolov11s) on CPU and GPU (if available), collecting their summaries.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
python scripts/benchmark_official.py \
  --data <data_yaml> \
  [--models name1 name2 …] \
  [--batch-size B] \
  [--output-base DIR]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
• Iterates over each model name (no .pt extension).
  • For CPU: creates runs/eval_official_<model>_cpu, invokes eval.py.
  • For GPU (if torch.cuda.is_available()): creates …_gpu, invokes eval.py.
  • Prints a warning if GPU is unavailable.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• --data (required) Path to dataset YAML (e.g. datasets/kitti50.yaml).
  • --models List of model names (default: yolov8s yolo11s).
  • --batch-size Inference batch size (default: 4).
  • --output-base Base directory under which to create eval_official_* folders (default: runs).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
# Benchmark yolov8s and yolov11s:
poetry run python scripts/benchmark_official.py \
  --data datasets/kitti50.yaml \
  --models yolov8s yolov11s \
  --batch-size 2 \
  --output-base runs/benchmark

docs.title: eval.py
docs.text: Evaluate a YOLO model on a validation set, compute mAP/precision/recall, benchmark FPS, and save a CSV summary.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
python scripts/eval.py \
  --weights <weights.pt> \
  --data <data_yaml> \
  [--device <device>] \
  [--batch-size B] \
  [--output-dir DIR]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
1. Loads model via YOLO(args.weights) and moves it to args.device.
  2. Runs model.val(...) to compute detection metrics (mAP, precision, recall).
  3. Scans the validation folder for images, runs model.predict(...) on each to measure FPS.
  4. Writes a summary.csv with rows: metric,value for precision, recall, map, fps.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• --weights (required) Path to .pt weights.
  • --data (required) Path to dataset YAML (must include val:).
  • --device Inference device, e.g. cpu or 0 (default: cpu).
  • --batch-size Batch size for the validation step (default: 16).
  • --output-dir Directory to save logs and outputs (default: runs/val).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
# Evaluate on KITTI-50 subset:
poetry run python scripts/eval.py \
  --weights yolov8n.pt \
  --data datasets/kitti50.yaml \
  --device cpu \
  --batch-size 4 \
  --output-dir runs/val/kitti50

docs.title: export.py
docs.text: Export a YOLO model to ONNX and verify the result with onnx.checker.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
python scripts/export.py \
  --weights <weights.pt> \
  --format onnx \
  [--dynamic] \
  [--int8] \
  [--output-dir DIR]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
1. Loads YOLO(args.weights).
  2. Calls model.export(format="onnx", dynamic=…, int8=…) into args.output_dir.
  3. Locates the .onnx file (even if nested) and copies it to the root of output_dir.
  4. Runs onnx.checker.check_model() to verify integrity.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• --weights, -w (required) Path to .pt weights.
  • --format, -f (required) Export format (only onnx supported).
  • --dynamic Enable dynamic input shapes.
  • --int8 Enable INT8 quantization.
  • --output-dir, -o Directory to save exported files (default: exports).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
# Export yolov8n.pt to ONNX with dynamic shapes:
poetry run python scripts/export.py \
  -w yolov8n.pt \
  -f onnx \
  --dynamic \
  -o exports/yolov8n

docs.title: fusion_offline.py
docs.text: Run YOLO detection + FusionEngine on a single image + pointcloud, printing fused results.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
python scripts/fusion_offline.py \
  --image <frame.png> \
  --pc <points.npy> \
  --weights <weights.pt> \
  [--min-points N]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
1. Loads an RGB image (.png/.jpg) into an array.
  2. Loads a LiDAR pointcloud (.npy, shape N×4).
  3. Runs YOLO(args.weights).predict(...) to get 2D detections.
  4. Instantiates FusionEngine with identity calibration and min_points.
  5. Calls fused = engine.fuse(detections, pc).
  6. Prints the number of fused detections and each dict.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• --image (required) Path to camera frame image.
  • --pc (required) Path to NumPy .npy pointcloud file.
  • --weights (required) Path to YOLO weights.
  • --min-points Minimum LiDAR points per box to keep (default: 3).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
poetry run python scripts/fusion_offline.py \
  --image tests/assets/000000.png \
  --pc tests/assets/000000.npy \
  --weights yolov8n.pt \
  --min-points 1

docs.title: main.py
docs.text: Live playback demo: stream KITTI or nuScenes, run 2D detection, fuse to 3D, track objects, and display.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: python scripts/main.py

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
• Uses DataStreamer to stream camera frames + LiDAR at ~10 Hz.
  • Loads a YOLO detector and a FusionEngine (identity calibration).
  • Applies SimpleTracker for per-frame tracking.
  • Displays an OpenCV window Overlay with annotated boxes, IDs, depth, point counts, and FPS.
  • Prints per-frame stats to stdout (used by tests).

Note: main.py is currently hard-coded to DATASET_NAME = "nuscenes". To use KITTI, edit that constant at the top of the script.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
• Adjust duration & rate by modifying the defaults in main(duration_sec, interval_sec).
  • Exit early: focus the window and press q.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
# Default run (10 s, 0.05 s interval):
poetry run python scripts/main.py

# For a longer run, edit:
#   main(duration_sec=30.0, interval_sec=0.05)

docs.title: overlay.py
docs.text: Helper function to draw detection & tracking overlays on an image.

docs.title: Function
docs.text: draw_overlay(frame: np.ndarray, tracks: List[Detection3D], fps: float) -> np.ndarray

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• frame H×W×3 RGB image (np.ndarray).

  • tracks List of Detection3D instances, each with:

  • track_id

  • class_id
  • confidence
  • box2d (x_min, y_min, x_max, y_max)
  • depth
  • num_points
  • fps Current processing frames-per-second.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
• Annotated BGR image (np.ndarray) ready for cv2.imshow():

  • Puts FPS in the top-left corner.

  • Draws blue bounding boxes and labels with ID, D:<depth>m, pts:<num_points>.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from scripts.overlay import draw_overlay
annotated = draw_overlay(rgb_frame, tracks, fps)
cv2.imshow("Overlay", annotated)

docs.title: train.py
docs.text: Train a YOLO model (v8, v11, etc.) on your dataset, with MLflow logging.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
python scripts/train.py \
  --model <model> \
  --data <data_yaml> \
  [--epochs N] \
  [--batch-size B] \
  [--img-size S] \
  [--output-dir DIR]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
1. Resolves --model into a .pt name (downloads pretrained if needed).
  2. Configures MLflow experiment (yolo_training) and autologging.
  3. Calls YOLO(model_spec).train(...).
  4. After training, finds the best checkpoint (best.pt) and logs it as an MLflow artifact.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• --model YOLO model name or path (yolov8n, yolov11s, or /path/to/custom.pt).
  • --data (required) Path to dataset YAML (must define train/val splits).
  • --epochs Number of training epochs (default: 50).
  • --batch-size Batch size (default: 16).
  • --img-size Input image resolution (default: 640).
  • --output-dir Directory under which to save runs (default: runs/train).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
# Train a tiny YOLOv8 model on KITTI-50 subset for 10 epochs:
poetry run python scripts/train.py \
  --model yolov8n \
  --data datasets/kitti50.yaml \
  --epochs 10 \
  --batch-size 8 \
  --img-size 640 \
  --output-dir runs/train/kitti50
